title: 98 The evolving metabolome of the porcine longissimus dorsi following a prenatal LPS challenge or vaccine
content:
Abstract
Inflammation induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) in gestating sows has been reported to alter the metabolome and skeletal muscle ultrastructure in offspring at weaning. This study aimed to evaluate the evolving metabolome in offspring skeletal muscle during postnatal life following a maternal lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge or commercial Escherichia coli vaccine during gestation. Sows were randomly assigned to a treatment beginning at 77 days of gestation: LPS (dosed at 2.5 µg/kg BW; n = 4), LitterGuard-LTC intramuscular vaccine (VAC; n = 3), or saline (CON; n = 3). Gilts from each prenatal treatment were necropsied at four timepoints during postnatal life: 3 d (LPS = 6; VAC = 6; CON = 6), 21 d (LPS = 5; VAC = 6; CON = 6), 100 d (LPS = 4; VAC = 5; CON = 6), and 200 d (LPS = 4; VAC = 6; CON = 9). At each time point, the longissimus dorsi muscle (LD) was snap-frozen in liquid nitrogen. Samples were homogenized into a powder and metabolites were extracted by weighing 50 mg of sample into a tube with 1.5 mL of 80% methanol and homogenized using a bead beater. Sample extract was dried with nitrogen gas then derivatized via methoximation and silylation. Untargeted metabolomics was conducted using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry. Mass spectral data were deconvoluted, aligned, and annotated using MS-DIAL. Total ion counts were median normalized and log10 transformed prior to analyses and data were analyzed using MetaboAnalyst by analysis of variance. Significance for all analyses was considered at FDR P ≤ 0.05. Metabolite analysis detected 191 features wherein 105 were annotated via linear retention index and mass spectral match. There were no differences (FDR P > 0.05) in the metabolome of gilts across prenatal treatment or the interaction of prenatal treatment × age. However, there was an effect of age (FDR P < 0.05) on the metabolomic profile of the LD. There were 63 differentially abundant metabolites across ages. Of the differentially abundant metabolites 16 were amino acids or their derivatives (FDR P ≤ 0.05). Five metabolites classified as neurotransmitters were differentially abundant (FDR P < 0.01). Four metabolites with roles in energy metabolism were differentially abundant (FDR P < 0.01). Three fatty acids were differentially abundant (FDR P ≤ 0.04). Finally, there were 6 saccharides which were differentially abundant (FDR P ≤ 0.01) across ages. The results of this study imply that prenatal exposure to LPS or a vaccine have no influence on the metabolome of female offspring skeletal muscle from birth through puberty. However, the metabolome of the LD is subject to changes during postnatal life with alterations in amino acid, fatty acid, and energy related metabolites in gilts from birth through puberty.
